dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of the us natural gas pipeline network in nisac s n able sandia national laboratories 2009 2010

description: Sandia National Laboratories' National Infrastructure Simulation and Analysis Center (NISAC) built an agent-based model of the US natural gas pipeline network inside N-ABLE, its Agent-Based Laboratory for Economics, which simulates firms and infrastructure together. Contents: the model is documented in two conference contributions by Paula S. Downes, Mark A. Ehlen and Greg E. Mackey: 'Modeling the U.S. Natural Gas Pipeline Network in the NISAC Agent-Based Laboratory for Economics (N-ABLE)' (September 2009, OSTI 1278765) and 'An agent based model of the U.S. natural gas pipeline network' (SAND2010-1438C, March 2010, OSTI 988499); neither record carries an abstract, and the Sandia keywords list engineers, natural gas, pipelines and safety. Coverage: the national interstate gas system. Format and access: publication records only; the model is an internal national laboratory tool. Licence and cost: not released; use would need Sandia. Caveats: the method, data and results were not readable from the cloud, so the description of what the agents represent follows N-ABLE's stated purpose, not the papers' text. It is an early example of agent-based network flow and cascading failure analysis for gas pipelines serving the economy. It relates to the National Pipeline Mapping System and PHMSA operator annual reports in the catalogue.
